newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: PORTUGAL PUBLIC DEBT SEEN BELOW 60 PCT GDP IN 2000.
newsitem.headline: PORTUGAL PUBLIC DEBT SEEN BELOW 60 PCT GDP IN 2000.

text.p: Portugal's public debt is expected to be below 60 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in the year 2000, Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco was quoted as saying.

"By carrying out a programme that has already been approved, public debt should fall below 60 percent (of GDP) in the year 2000," Sousa Franco told "Homem Magazine" in an interview published on Friday.
He said Portugal's continuing privatisation programme was expected to cut public debt.
The government has forecast public debt as a proportion of GDP should drop to 64.1 percent in 1997 and 62.9 percent in 1998.
Sousa Franco said Portugal's privatisation programme has been a success and had helped transform Portugal into a developed market from its previous status as an emerging market.
